styles.label: Culture
styles.blurb: Temples, markets and colonial streets in Fort and Pettah.

styles.label: Food
styles.blurb: Rice and curry, hoppers, kottu and street snacks.

styles.label: Beach
styles.blurb: City seafront walks and a train ride to Mount Lavinia.

stays.why: Walk to the old colonial buildings, the lighthouse and the station. Handy for the airport road and trains.
Cheapest base and right in the bazaar chaos. Basic rooms; noisy and busy streets.
Central and modern: shops, restaurants and the Galle Face seafront walk nearby.
Beach suburb south of the city. Quieter, with a train ride into Fort.

food: Try rice and curry, egg hoppers, string hoppers and kottu roti. Small local cafés are cheapest.
Eat short eats: fish cutlets, rolls and samosas from bakeries, about Rs 50–150 each.
Pettah and Fort have cheap Indian and Sri Lankan eateries; check hygiene and go where locals queue.
Seafood is good along the coast; ask the price per kilo before ordering.
Tea is everywhere. Order a plain milk tea and expect it very sweet unless you say otherwise.
more_time: Swap a city day for a train ride south to Mount Lavinia for the beach and a seafood lunch.
Add a half day in Pettah: the Red Mosque, the markets and the old streets.
Take a longer day trip to Galle or Kandy by train; book seats early and check times on the day.

recommend.why: Two nights covers Fort, Pettah and the seafront at an easy pace; add a night for a beach or day trip.

month_notes: January: one of the driest, sunniest months. Great for walking Fort and Pettah.
February: dry and warm. Good all-round month for sightseeing.
March: rain picks up. Carry a light rain jacket for afternoon showers.
April: wet, with about 25 rain days. Plan indoor sights and short outings.
May: the wettest month, around 30 rain days. Expect heavy downpours; keep plans flexible.
June: still very wet. Short dry windows; check the sky before long walks.
July: wet and slightly cooler. Good for museums and covered markets.
August: coolest highs around 28°C but still rainy. Pack a rain layer.
September: similar to August: mild and wet. Fewer crowds at sights.
October: very wet again, about 29 rain days. Avoid tight outdoor schedules.
November: rain eases. Better for walking and the seafront.
December: drier and warmer. A good month for city sightseeing and the beach.

climate_guide.summary: Tropical and hot all year, with a long wet season from April to October and drier, sunnier months from December to February.

items.title: Best time: December to February
items.text: Warm days around 30–31°C and the fewest rain days, about 11 a month. Best for walking and the beach.

items.title: Wet season: April to October
items.text: Rain on 25–30 days a month, heaviest in May. Expect short heavy downpours, often in the afternoon.

items.title: Hot and humid year-round
items.text: Highs stay near 28–31°C and lows near 23–25°C. Humidity makes it feel hotter.

items.title: Always carry rain cover
items.text: Even in dry months a shower is possible. A small umbrella or light rain jacket helps.

items.title: What to pack
items.text: Light breathable clothes, sandals, sunscreen and a hat. A light layer for air-conditioned places.

items.title: Dress for temples
items.text: Cover shoulders and knees at religious sites. Remove shoes where asked.

transit.best: Tuk-tuks and ride apps for most trips; buses are cheap but slow.

modes.text: No metro or tram. Don't plan around rail inside the city.
Buses are the main public transport. Fares start at Rs 30, pay the conductor onboard.
PickMe and Uber both work well. Tuk-tuks are everywhere; agree a price or use a meter taxi.
Not covered in our checked facts. Most visitors use tuk-tuks, apps and buses instead.
Works in Fort and Pettah, but pavements are uneven. Use a tuk-tuk for longer hops.
Commuter trains run on four lines, including the coastal line to Mount Lavinia.
Everywhere and easy to flag. Agree the price first or ask for the meter.
